cells.tense: You are standing in what you grew, and you know it belongs to you.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you've cared for longest and tell someone what it took. Let the telling finish it, not start another task.
cells.core:
Something you've been caring for has come in, and you can stand in it without gripping. The work is producing. You're not clawing at the result, not already turning to the next plot, and that steadiness is what the years bought you. When this is healthy, you hold what arrived and stay gentle with it — the result doesn't have to be defended, or topped, or explained to anyone.

The bend is quieter than that. You carry a lot without comment, and there's a habit of treating what's arrived as a pit stop. Let one piece of it be yours to keep. Say to one person what it took to get here, and stop when you've said it. Nothing to fix after.
cells.sheetLine: The slow work landed. Let yourself stand in it.
cells.verb: tending what you've grown until it bears more than you planted
cells.place: in the forward pull of a life that's already moving somewhere

cells.tense: You are already living in a harvest that hasn't finished growing yet.
cells.ask: Name one thing you'd planned for next season and leave that ground empty this year. Put it on paper where you'll see it.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward results that haven't arrived, and your momentum is the thing doing the pushing. One project becomes the next before the first has cooled. What you already have goes unenjoyed while you're out starting more. A lot of your effort lands on ground that isn't ready to receive it, and the pushing is starting to cost what was growing.

Sitting still won't hold you, so rest isn't the fix. What's missing is one field left alone on purpose. Give it a season and find out you don't starve when you stop. That hunger you're moving from is a guess, not a fact about your life.
cells.sheetLine: You're farming the next yield before this one's in.

cells.tense: You are still standing in a doorway you walked through a while back.
cells.ask: Point at one direction you want and say it to someone plainly. Take the first small step today, before you feel ready.
cells.core:
There was a heading you used to have, and picking one stopped being easy. So you stopped pointing and kept working anyway. The effort still runs, but it runs without a destination, and that costs more than any goal ever did. On the other side of this, the work has somewhere to arrive — you put your effort behind a name you chose.

Don't try to recharge by forcing the drive back. Lift your eyes to something worth moving toward, one light you'd actually steer by, and let it pull. Choosing comes before feeling chosen more often than the other way. Once the direction is set, the momentum follows on its own, without being shoved.
cells.sheetLine: The effort still runs, but the aim went quiet.

cells.tense: You are already moving people forward and you keep calling it the schedule.
cells.ask: Write down who you get moving and what it costs you, using no word for busy. Read it, then say out loud that you chose it.
cells.core:
You run the forward motion for more than just yourself. You get plans off the ground, you carry people past the stuck part, you spot the next step early. And you file the whole thing under things that happen, the way you'd file traffic or rain. Done well, the direction is claimed — the one doing the pushing signs for it.

That's the gap worth closing. Own one push you gave, out loud, naming yourself as the one who did it. Nothing about what you do changes. Only who it counts as — and that's a release, not a loss.
cells.sheetLine: It's moving because you move it. Say so.
